subject: James Watson mentioned you on the company "Spyne"
text:
James Watson mentioned you on the company "Spyne"
@Charlotte Decaudaveine @Oscar Evans @Leo Leclercq
Attendees: Praveen Agarwal (Head of Operations), Sati (Head of Product) 
1) Background to Opportunity:
Spyne AI is a fast-growing vertical SaaS company specializing in automotive image and video processing, converting raw vehicle images into studio-quality assets. 
They currently offer merchandising (image generation, 360-degree stitches, promotional videos) and are expanding into AI-powered vehicle inspections (identifying damages, scratches, etc., from video). Their AI models currently achieve ~94% accuracy for existing products.
Praveen's team manages the operations around cataloging images via AI, with manual intervention for failed cases, and crucially, handles data annotation (masking, labeling) for AI training. They are currently using a combination of in-house tooling and a few external annotation tools. Praveen had a previous, albeit unmemorable, call with Encord last year.
This opportunity arises as Spyne AI seeks to significantly improve their AI model accuracy (target 98-99%) and requires a hug increase in data ("millions of files") for this improvement, which their current setup struggles to deliver at scale. The upcoming "inspections" product will further exacerbate this data volume and complexity challenge, especially with video data.
2) Needs:
Improve AI Model Accuracy: Primary driver is to increase AI accuracy from ~94% to 98-99% for existing and new products. This necessitates a robust data engine.
Handle Massive Data Volumes: Current and future needs demand processing "millions of data" (images and upcoming videos) for training and iteration, which is currently a bottleneck.
Efficient & Scalable Data Annotation: They need a solution that can efficiently manage the annotation of these high volumes, including complex tasks like masking and segmentation.
Support for Video Data (New Product): The new "inspections" product will rely heavily on video dat

subject: Re: Nice to meet on Friday
text:
Hey James,
Thank you for reaching out to schedule a follow-up call. Not going to do the call this week as I would like to have more info and clarity first. What would the purpose be of this, for a demo?

We currently anticipate requiring approximately 5,000–10,000 hours of audio files to be annotated over the next 12 months. This could evolve rapidly as we onboard indie artists. For growth projections, we expect a 20–30% increase in annotation volume over the year. Is this sufficient for you guys?

We can enrich the labels with existing metadata from the songs including things like BPM, key. This might prove helpful for annotators. We require more manual intervention for subjective info like energy (On a 1-10 scale) and keywords that will form the basis of training packs. For example a film score dataset might include songs that are instrumental but also listenable on their own independent of being synced.

Anything else I’m missing? I am new to data labelling in general so any guidance is appreciated.

Byron Polley ❖ www.polyphonic.io <https://polyphonic.io/> ❖ +27 83 286 5231

subject: RE: Pricing for labeling services
text:
Hi Arisha and Alyssa,

I just added 3 example projects with accelerate@encord.com<mailto:accelerate@encord.com> as a manger. For each project I did one annotation that is in Review as an example. We don’t have annotation instruction PDFs (we can make them) but I’ll list the standards in these examples:

  1.  Example expert grading | Encord<https://app.encord.com/projects/view/5aca702f-9080-4bbc-afec-a123eae80f93/settings> – This is the type of project we would want an eye care professional to grade. It includes labeling:
     *   Diabetic retinopathy (DR) severity with options - [“less than moderate”, “moderate”, “vision threatening”, “ungradable”]. If talking to a doctor I believe we use a standard of ETDRS level 35 or above for *moderate*, not sure for vision threatening.
     *   Diabetic macular edema (DME) presence - True/False. If talking to a doctor, either center involved or non-center involved DME.
     *   Image Quality – whether the image is good quality, binary Good/Bad. This is distinct from “ungradable” because an image can be very low quality but if disease is obvious it may still be gradable. This is something we also have non-expert graders label
     *   Laser scaring – whether there is visible laser scaring from past treatment for DR, binary True/False. We also would potentially have non-experts label this.
  2.  Non-expert objects annotation | Encord<https://app.encord.com/projects/view/43285f5c-ff4f-427b-aac3-825afd12541e/summary> – This is a project we would have a non-expert annotate the location of specific biomarkers/landmarks in a fundus image
     *   Fovea center – center of fovea landmark [see example]
     *   Optic disc (OD) center – center of optic disk landmark
     *   Fixation – which landmark is in the center of the image: [“Fovea”, “OD”, “Center”, “Unknown”] where “Center” means between the OD and fovea, and Unknown is anything not in the list.
     *   Orientation – Is this a left or right eye (optic disc is to the right of the
